# SCA allowlist (Software Composition Analysis)
#
# One GitHub advisory (GHSA) id per line. The CI "sca-frontend" job
# (.github/workflows/ci.yml -> .github/scripts/sca-audit.mjs) fails the build on
# ANY high or critical advisory in a production dependency UNLESS its GHSA id is
# listed here. This is the SCA equivalent of the frontend-app lint
# `--max-warnings=46` cap: it freezes the currently-known backlog so it cannot
# grow, while a separate remediation effort works it down. Any brand-new high or
# critical advisory fails CI immediately.
#
# Rules:
#   - Add an id here ONLY after a human decision: the advisory is a false
#     positive for our usage, or it is not yet fixable without a breaking upgrade
#     that is scheduled separately. Never add one just to make CI green.
#   - Every entry needs a one-line justification and, if fixable, a remediation
#     pointer (issue / "npm audit fix" / target version).
#   - When an advisory is fixed upstream and no longer appears, the job prints it
#     as a "safe to remove" note (it does not fail). Prune it then.
#   - Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. Anything after `#` on a line is a
#     comment, so you may annotate inline: GHSA-xxxx  # why
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Seeded 2026-07-24 from the state of main when the gate was introduced (#117).
# Worked to empty on 2026-07-31 by #532: all 10 seeded highs were remediated by
# dependency upgrades (next 15.5.22, postcss 8.5.25, sharp 0.35.3,
# @opentelemetry/propagator-jaeger 2.10.0, axios 1.19.0, brace-expansion
# 1.1.18 / 2.1.4). The gate now enforces with an EMPTY allowlist: any high or
# critical advisory in a production dependency fails CI. Do not re-seed this
# file just to make CI green; add an id only after a human decision per the
# rules above.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Re-seeded 2026-08-03: the #532 dependency upgrades (next 15.5.22, sharp
# 0.35.3, propagator-jaeger 2.10.0, postcss 8.5.25) break Azure SWA deploys.
# Every deploy-landing run since #542 merged failed with "Web app warm up
# timed out" (600s; healthy warm-up is ~273s). A 7-run bisect on branch
# fix/landing-warmup-sharp-bisect proved it: the pre-#542 dependency set
# deployed green twice; every partial revert (each package individually
# cleared, every pair) failed. The set below pins back the four packages and
# accepts their advisories with the per-line justifications. Remediation
# tracker: issue #566 (re-attempt each upgrade individually against SWA).
# The frontend-app remediations from #532 (axios, brace-expansion) are
# unaffected and stay upgraded.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
GHSA-45rx-2jwx-cxfr  # jaeger DoS via malformed header; only if JaegerPropagator is the registered global propagator. Ours never is: instrumentation.ts uses useAzureMonitor (W3C TraceContext+Baggage). Do not set OTEL_PROPAGATORS=jaeger while pinned. Security-audit verdict 2026-08-03: zero exploitability.
GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q  # postcss arbitrary file read via sourceMappingURL: build-time only, postcss processes our own Tailwind CSS in CI, never attacker-controlled CSS.
GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849  # postcss path traversal in source-map auto-loading: same build-time-own-CSS scoping as above.
GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x  # next SSRF in Server Actions on custom servers: zero 'use server' directives in frontend-public and no custom server.
GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj  # next DoS in App Router Server Actions: zero 'use server' directives in frontend-public.
GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4  # next SSRF in rewrites via attacker-controlled destination: our only redirect destination is the static apex-to-www hostname in next.config.ts.
GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj  # sharp/libvips CVEs: image optimizer decodes only our pinned storage account + media.altarwed.com (remotePatterns narrowing, issue #98); upload path requires an authenticated couple session.
